art_version_or_none: none (art_brief v1: no_art_required=true; existing recycle_sorting.jpg/food_waste.jpg/compost_to_farm.jpg reused as-is, no new assets; schoolLunch.ts's recycle-lunch entry's tools: [] emptied since the custom component renders its own tool UI, matching the delay_recover/hotel_receive precedent)
d_preserved_statement: Unchanged from implementation_v1.json -- the mechanic itself (sortOutLogic.ts's PROPERTIES/TOOLS/CORRECT_TOOL/ITEMS/newSession/sessionWin, the disclosure-gated single-commit-per-item flow, Gate G/H) was not touched by this repair; impl review r1 found 0 blockers against the mechanic itself (logic_matches_design_sim, brute_force_genuinely_closed, item_identity_neutral_and_coherent, no_exclusivity_overclaim, no_mismatch_partial_effect_overclaim, label_leak_closed, gate_g_correct, gate_h_correct, disclosure_gating_correct all confirmed true).

repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.BATCHING_STATE_CLOSURE (HIGH): v1 split per-item UI into 3 separate useState pieces (openedItems: Set, selectedTool: Partial<Record>, appliedTool: Partial<Record>). selectTool's updater guarded on the render-scope `appliedTool[id]` (a sibling state, read outside its own setter) and apply's updater guarded on the render-scope `selectedTool[id]` (also a sibling state) -- neither was fully self-contained within its own setState updater, contradicting the batching-safe pattern the implementation claimed to follow. Fixed by consolidating all 3 fields into a single `itemUI: Record<ItemId, {opened, selectedTool, appliedTool}>` state object, matching HotelReceiveGame.tsx's groupUI pattern exactly -- openItem/selectTool/apply now each derive entirely from their own setItemUI((prev) => ...) updater's `prev[id]`, with no read of the outer-scope `itemUI` variable inside any updater body.
repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.QA_REGRESSION_VACUOUS x2 (MEDIUM): gameplay-qa-sort-out.mjs's batching check previously asserted `fn.includes('if (prev[id] || !selectedTool[id]) return prev;')`, which literally required (and therefore passed on) the exact stale-closure pattern it claimed to forbid. Rewritten to assert the updater body contains no bare `itemUI[` / `itemUI)` reference at all, for openItem/selectTool/apply independently -- verified non-vacuous by deliberately reintroducing the exact r1 bug pattern (apply() reading outer-scope `itemUI[id].selectedTool` instead of `prev[id].selectedTool`) and confirming the check correctly fails, then restoring and confirming it passes again. The neutral-identity check previously counted '📦 異物' occurrences across the playing AND reflecting branches combined (>=2 total), so a new fixed identity introduced in only one branch could still pass if the other branch supplied enough matches -- rewritten into two independent checks, one scoped to each branch, each requiring exactly the neutral label within that branch alone.
repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.IMPLEMENTATION_QA_EVIDENCE_INACCURATE (M: implementation_qa_v1.json's first_5_seconds claim ('カードをタップすると開き') was corrected in implementation_qa_v2.json to name the actual tap target precisely (the dx-more '？'/'－' button in the card header), matching the already-shipped, already-reviewed identical pattern in DelayRecoverGame.tsx/HotelReceiveGame.tsx rather than implying the whole card row is tappable.
repair_v2_impl_review_r1_findings_addres.MOBILE_UNIFORMITY_UNSUPPORTED (MEDIUM): implementation_qa_v1.json's mobile_375 claim was corrected in implementation_qa_v2.json: the actually-true and actually-achieved property is that the 3 CLOSED item cards are visually uniform to EACH OTHER (no card's closed state hints at its property), not that a closed card and an opened card have equal height -- an opened card naturally growing taller to fit its observation text and 3 tool buttons is normal, expected, and matches every other Q1 game's disclosure-card pattern; it was never the actual design intent nor a meaningful claim, and no other shipped Q1 game satisfies it either.

browser_verification_v2: Re-ran the full manual playthrough in the dev preview after the state-consolidation refactor, in a fresh browser tab (to rule out stale console-buffer artifacts from a deliberate mid-repair bug-reintroduction test): full success path (all 3 items' properties read correctly, matching tools applied) reached the 'done' branch with the correct result text and resolution scene; deliberately mismatching all 3 items reached the 'reflecting' branch, correctly re-presented all 3 items' observations and the actual applied tool read-only, and required a full reflection pick set before enabling 先へ進む. Zero console errors in a freshly-opened tab for both paths.
